summary.title: Joins 13 Ways
summary.one_liner: Learn thirteen different ways to understand and implement a relational inner join, from nested loops and flatMap to type checking, graph paths, and ring products.
keywords: partial order least upper bound join
what is a join in plain english
takeaways: A join can be seen as a lookup that adds redundant data from a normalized table back onto a fact table.
A join equals a nested loop over rows filtered by a predicate, or a flatMap over one relation with a filtered second relation.
Logic-based views treat a join as the smallest model satisfying the implication, and as the largest acceptable relation that invents no new information.
Joins also appear in the Set monad, Rust trait typechecking, graph path enumeration, and polynomial ring products.
summary.summary: The post explains the relational inner join by presenting many equivalent perspectives, each illustrated with small example tables (users and countries). It starts with the practical view of normalization and lookups, then covers nested loop implementations over rows and columns, flatMap and SQL LATERAL joins, and the N+1 query problem. More theoretical angles follow: Datalog-style minimal models, Rust trait typechecking, a Set-monad-style Rel container in JavaScript, the largest acceptable relation, a partial-order join, and a polynomial ring product representation.
